|**2026-11-19**|**OCLDA-GS: Object-Centric Local Deformation-Aware Gaussian Streaming**|Ashim Dahal et.al.|Streaming 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for online reconstruction of dynamic scenes from multi-view videos for Free Viewpoint Video (FVV). Current time and storage efficient methods rely on selecting a subset of anchor Gaussians and neighborhood interpolation for fast streamable 3DGS. However, these methods can overlook object-specific motion and introduce inconsistencies near object boundaries. We propose OCLDA-GS, an object-centric streaming framework that dynamically reallocates object and motion-aware Gaussian anchors to allocate anchor Gaussian support for objects undergoing large motion while at the same time, restricting the gaussian neighborhood within object groups for more precise object boundaries. Furthermore, it estimates object-wise rigid transformations (e.g. a hand moving) and leverages these estimates to learn per-anchor local deformation correction for small deformations (e.g. wrinkles on a shirt). Then, we conduct experiments on three dynamic multi-view video datasets and demonstrate improvements over the previous baselines alongside improved quality between refinement timesteps. Under matched refinement budgets, our method improves PSNR over Instant Gaussian Stream (IGS) by 0.169 dB on N3DV, 0.202 dB on Meeting Room and +0.199 on Google Immersive, while reducing the mean PSNR drop between refinement timesteps by 9.2% and 13.8% in N3DV and Meeting Room, respectively.|[2611.23416](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23416)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Autoregressive View Model**|Jensen (Jinghao) et.al.|We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. We fine-tune a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation. We then tune a causal model on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift. We scale training to approximately 8M scenes and video clips. We evaluate generation capacity and scene persistence across benchmarks for camera control, text control, visual quality, dynamics, sparse and 4D reconstruction, and long-horizon consistency. The results demonstrate that AVM adapts to diverse input and output settings through one in-context interface.|[2611.23417](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23417)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs**|Haisheng Fu et.al.|Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Its three design constants were fixed once on labeled COCO data, and a new model or resolution needs only unlabeled questions. Across eight VLMs, WhereBits matches the pointing accuracy of box-tuned layers on COCO and RefCOCO and ranks target tokens better. This advantage holds on a held-out model family and at higher resolutions. Its COCO pointing accuracy is 0.72, against 0.22 for mean attention. In training-free zoom-in, its crops raise V* accuracy by 6.0 points under forced-choice evaluation.|[2611.23432](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23432)|
|**2026-11-19**|**TransFIRA+: Transfer Learning for Biometric Recognizability Assessment**|Allen Tu et.al.|Biometric recognition in surveillance, video, and web imagery must contend with extreme variation in pose, blur, illumination, occlusion, and distance, where visual quality metrics fail to predict whether inputs are recognizable to the deployed encoder. Existing face image quality assessment methods rely on visual heuristics, curated annotations, or costly generative pipelines, leaving their predictions detached from the encoder's decision geometry. We introduce TransFIRA, a lightweight framework that grounds recognizability directly in embedding space. TransFIRA derives class-center similarity (CCS) and class-center angular separation (CCAS) from a pretrained encoder's embeddings and learns to predict them from images without quality annotations. Using predicted CCS for template weighting and CCAS>0 as a natural filtering threshold yields state-of-the-art face verification performance on BRIAR, raising TAR at $10^{-6}$ FMR from 0.085 with uniform averaging to 0.598. The predicted scores also reveal how image degradations affect encoder-specific recognizability. TransFIRA+ extends this framework to cross-camera multimodal person identification in untrimmed surveillance video. In this setting, body recognizability scores saturate within a narrow range, making direct weighting effectively uniform. We introduce a post-hoc sigmoid calibration that transforms these saturated scores into informative weights without retraining. After calibration, the BRIAR-trained TransFIRA predictor improves fused face and body identification on two unseen multi-camera datasets, outperforming detector-confidence weighting and uncalibrated CCS-rank weighting. Together, TransFIRA and TransFIRA+ demonstrate that encoder-grounded recognizability generalizes across biometric modalities and recognition settings.|[2611.23442](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23442)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones**|Michael Schroeder et.al.|Compact convolutional backbones such as EfficientNet achieve strong parameter efficiency through local depthwise separable convolutions, yet two structural questions remain central to hybrid design: where does global self-attention improve recognition over pure convolution, and can repeated blocks share weights without losing representational capacity? We investigate both questions on ImageNet-1k (50,000-image validation) using controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments. First, we show that wrapping a classification backbone in multi-scale feature pyramids (BiFPN) fails to outperform a plain MBConv trunk (69.99% - 71.81% vs. 72.86% plain B0) until paired with stage attention (73.15%). In contrast, keeping the MBConv trunk intact and inserting lightweight zero-gated residual self-attention adapters at stages P3 (28x28 windowed), P4 (14x14 global), and P5 (7x7 global) reaches 74.02% standalone and outperforms a bit-for-bit matched plain-B0 control by +0.954 percentage points (73.88% vs. 72.92%) across an 88-epoch stateless replay schedule, with learned attention amplitude rising monotonically with semantic depth (27.2% at P3 -> 45.4% at P4 -> 66.3% at P5). Second, we evaluate recurrent weight sharing across repeated MBConv blocks with pass-specific BatchNorm statistics (+1,536 parameters per pass). While post-hoc kernel averaging degrades accuracy to 17.03% and single-template stage tying (-27.6% parameters) plateaus at 66.10%, alternating two shared block templates ([B1, A, B, A]) in Stage 6 cuts total model parameters by 10.9% (582K weights) and recovers by +10.82 points in a single epoch to 70.92% (-1.84 points vs. unshared control).|[2611.23446](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23446)|
|**2026-11-19**|**NIRJALA: Draining the Sea out of Gaussian Splatting with Three-Path Optics and Reversible Physics**|Latchan Chhetri et.al.|Water does not just tint an underwater photograph; it rewrites it. Each pixel mixes attenuated scene radiance, backscattered light, and scene light scattered forward on its way to the camera, and many combinations of scene and water explain the same pixels. Most Gaussian-splatting methods for underwater scenes model only the first two effects and remove the water by dividing by a transmission that decays exponentially with range, so their inversion gain grows without bound. We present NIRJALA (Sanskrit for "without water"), a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that recovers water-free appearance and geometry together. TRIVENI, a three-path image formation model, adds a range-saturating forward-scattering term to direct transmission and backscatter; we prove that this keeps the inversion gain bounded at every range and bound how errors in the estimated backscatter and attenuation propagate into the recovered colours. PRATIBIMBA, a reversible physics anchor, ties a flexible neural water model to a ten-parameter physical model in both directions, so scene content cannot hide inside the water. SAMARASA collects the physics-informed objectives, including a range-binned colour prior. To score water removal against ground truth, we built SAJALA ("with water"), a 30-scene suite path-traced in Blender Cycles with water-free images, depth, and normals under controlled water colour and turbidity. On SAJALA, NIRJALA raises PSNR from 24.34 to 24.76 dB and lowers depth AbsRel from 0.109 to 0.091 against the strongest baseline; on real SeaThru-NeRF scenes it lowers LPIPS from 0.194 to 0.175 while rendering at 44 FPS. We also discuss where appearance metrics and geometry disagree underwater, and the limits of our evaluation.|[2611.23450](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23450)|
|**2026-11-19**|**mmTherm: Absolute 3D Human Pose Estimation from Low-Resolution Thermal Images and mmWave Radar**|Zhaoxin Chang et.al.|Absolute 3D human pose estimation (HPE) aims to recover both a person's body pose and their global position in 3D space. Privacy-preserving millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides distance and direction measurement capabilities, but its sparse point clouds make HPE under-constrained. Low-resolution thermal imaging can provide complementary observations of body direction and structure. However, our evaluation shows that a strong feature-level fusion baseline loses much of its localization and HPE advantage when generalizing to unseen subjects, with radial localization becoming less accurate than a radar-only baseline. Motivated by this finding, we introduce mmTherm, a lightweight framework that explicitly incorporates the complementary geometric properties of thermal imaging and mmWave radar. It combines body structure and joint directions estimated from thermal images with range information from radar to localize the body and reconstruct its 3D pose. Experiments on OctoNet show that mmTherm reduces cross-user absolute joint error by 33% and root localization error by 38% relative to the strongest corresponding baselines, while requiring substantially fewer parameters and less computation at inference.|[2611.23477](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23477)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining**|Faidra Patsatzi et.al.|Training 3D vision-language models (VLMs) on large medical imaging datasets collected across institutions is constrained by data quality. Vast, uncurated pools of image-report pairs are characterized by redundancy, class imbalance, and cross-institutional heterogeneity. We address this challenge of data curation for improving 3D VLM pretraining by proposing an offline, training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe. Our approach leverages a small, high-quality reference set to independently extract quality signals for each modality of a large, uncurated pool and merges them through a rank-aggregation step into a single ranking that guides sample selection. We validate this method on datasets comprising 35k 3D abdominal CT volume-report pairs from two institutions and 58k 2D chest X-ray image-report pairs. On 3D CT, using our reference-guided data curation strategy, our curated model matches the zero-shot disease classification performance of a state-of-the-art baseline (Merlin) while using $3.3\times$ less training data and a reference set of 5k samples. On 2D chest X-rays, our method yields a curated model that matches or exceeds the zero-shot disease classification performance of a model trained on the full pool while using up to $10\times$ less training data and a reference set of only 74 samples. Ablations show that the selection is stable under resampling of the reference, that smaller reference sets still outperform random sampling, and that label rebalancing does not improve performance. To support reproducibility, we release our code.|[2611.23484](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23484)|
|**2026-11-19**|**GRID-UAV: Geometry and Ray-depth Integrated Decision-making for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles**|Anas Anwarul Haq Khan et.al.|Vision-language-action models (VLAs) encode images with 2D encoders that capture little 3D structure. A common approach is to feed the policy estimated depth, but a UAV chooses its own altitude, must judge distances tens of meters away, where monocular depth is less reliable, and must relate its forward and downward views. On long aerial routes, adding depth features directly brings no significant gain (42.5% vs. 42.6% success), so we study how 3D information should be given to the policy. Analyzing flight failures, we find that two forms of 3D grounding fail in opposite ways: explicit 3D lifting of depth collides less on the way but more often fails to finish at the target, while implicit alignment with a 3D geometry model finishes more often but collides more. We propose GRID, which combines both: (1) it lifts monocular depth into ray-corrected 3D positions in the UAV's frame for both cameras, and (2) during training only, it aligns its visual features with a frozen multi-view geometry model, at no inference cost. GRID adding explicit lifting to implicit alignment significantly increases how often the policy reaches the target ($61.5\% \rightarrow 69.5\%$, $p<0.001$), and adding implicit alignment to explicit lifting significantly increases how often it completes the task once there ($57.7\% \rightarrow 61.4\%$, $p<0.05$). On TravelUAV (3,005 test episodes), GRID achieves the best success rate on every split, with relative gains over the state of the art of 9.5% (seen), 17.1% (unseen objects) and 25.4% (unseen map).|[2611.23491](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23491)|
|**2026-11-19**|**MedHarness: A Unified Budgeted Runtime for Reliable Medical Imaging Agents**|Haofan Wu et.al.|Medical imaging agents already return answers on heterogeneous imaging surfaces, yet deployment still faces a limited verification budget where each wrong accept can harm clinical trust. When a thin check and a deeper evidence pass disagree on the same case, deciding when to stop, open more evidence, repair, or reject without a shared controller remains ill-posed. Tool-using workflows often lock a surface-specific evidence order per dataset, or a private always-open full-depth verification path; those pipelines stay costly, leave many wrong accepts, and cannot share one controller across modalities. We present MedHarness, a registered multi-surface runtime reliability layer that reformulates post-answer control as shared decision-object attachment after a proposer's initial prediction. Under Shared Decision Object, Minimum-Sufficient Verification, and Intermediate Repair, one shared policy with surface recipe adapters lets a new imaging surface join the same stop / open-evidence / repair / reject controller by recipe registration. On a 512-case live pool, MedHarness cuts wrong accepts versus a full-verification baseline by about 47% and raises accepted accuracy to 83.2% vs. 72.9% at 86.1% coverage versus full release under that baseline. On a failure-enriched multi-surface stress ranking, the same controller cuts estimated remote service calls per case by about 71% versus that baseline under a matched context-load setting. A held-out three-surface check and an alternate language-model transfer keep the same control ordering. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MedHarness-paper-release-A7F3/.|[2611.23501](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23501)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Trust the Ray, Not the Depth: Ray-Lateral Agreement for Multi-View 3D Human Pose Fusion**|Farnoosh Koleini et.al.|Put a monocular mesh estimator behind every camera of a calibrated rig, and the reconstructed bodies land a meter or more apart. The cause is geometric: each estimate sits at the depth implied by a focal length the network assumed, not the one the camera has. Its error therefore points almost entirely along its own viewing ray, and the calibration tells us that direction exactly. To address this, we introduce the Ray-Lateral Agreement (RLA), which follows one rule: trust the ray, not the depth. RLA first slides every estimate along its own rays, which removes the depth bias and leaves the shape untouched. It then fuses the views one point at a time, under a Gaussian error whose precision follows each viewing ray. The maximum-likelihood solution is closed-form, interpolates between averaging and midpoint triangulation, and stays well conditioned where triangulation is singular. Robustness is the harder half, because correct views also disagree along their rays. Any weight built on the full residual therefore punishes good views together with bad ones. Ray-lateral agreement instead scores every view, at every point, by its residual across that view's own ray alone. We evaluated RLA on multi-camera public benchmark datasets. Across two, three, and four cameras and three per-view pose estimators, RLA consistently achieves lower worst-case error than all triangulation baselines.|[2611.23513](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23513)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Beyond the Sink Token: Sink-Guided Key Editing in Vision-Language Models**|Hui Zhu et.al.|In vision-language models (VLMs), a few sink tokens attract a disproportionate share of attention. While previous studies have examined why these tokens attract attention, we investigate how the sink-key direction affects attention to image and question tokens. Across four probed VLMs, boosting the magnitude of positive sink-aligned components increases attention on average, whereas boosting negative components decreases it; these responses persist through later layers. This identifies the native sink key as a reference for controlling attention beyond its own position. Motivated by this finding, we propose SHRINK, a training-free method that partially reduces sink-aligned components across visible keys during generation. On nine benchmarks under sampled reasoning, it improves mean accuracy by 5.1 and 2.7 percentage points on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B, with smaller gains on the other two main models, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Gemma-3-4B. Beyond SHRINK, rescaling sink-aligned key components can replace the attention operations of two existing attention-steering methods, GIFT and ACG, with comparable accuracy on hallucination benchmarks.|[2611.23516](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23516)|
|**2026-11-19**|**ORGANIC3D: Grounding 3D CT Vision Language Models in Organ Level Image Text Coupling**|Zelong Liu et.al.|Vision language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in 3D computed tomography (CT) classification, but high accuracy does not reflect whether their predictions rely on the correct anatomical evidence. We introduce ORGANIC3D, a framework for evaluating and improving organ level image text alignment through controlled anatomical interventions. Our benchmark assesses 12 vision encoder checkpoints and 7 generative VLMs using matched patient comparisons, organ erasure, lesion replacement, and laterality perturbations, revealing substantial alignment failures even among top performing models. To learn organ level image text correspondence, ORGANIC3D aligns each finding sentence with the anatomy aware image features and trains on edited scans to anchor this alignment in the organ's image evidence. We further extend this framework to generative VLMs, promoting evidence dependent question answering and report generation. Trained exclusively on public data, ORGANIC3D achieves SOTA classification AUROC on CTRATE, Merlin, and the heldout RADChestCT dataset and reaches 77% laterality accuracy, compared with at most 66% for prior models. Its generative VLM matches or exceeds all evaluated publicly released VLMs on visual question answering, achieves the highest report accuracy, and retracts 96 to 99% of target organ findings after organ removal, versus a maximum of 69% for other models. Together, these results establish ORGANIC3D as a framework for testing whether 3D CT vision language models ground their predictions in anatomical evidence and for improving organ level alignment alongside predictive accuracy.|[2611.23529](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23529)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Layer-Matched Sparse Attention for Low-Redundancy 3D Reconstruction**|Sammam Mahdi et.al.|VGGT reconstructs cameras and geometry from unposed images in one pass, but its global attention grows quadratically with the number of views. Training-free accelerators thin this attention and work well on redundant video, but lose pose accuracy when views share little geometry. This paper traces these losses to two kinds of cross-view information that a uniform sparse approximation can fail to preserve together: diffuse layers aggregate distributed context, whereas matching layers depend on query-specific interactions that carry little attention mass. A per-layer statistic measures the log-mass missed by a mean token. Its row-free proxy is the logit variance, and it selects the estimator for each layer. Diffuse layers use shared, importance-sampled hub keys, with log-weights that make the softmax numerator and denominator unbiased. Matching layers stay exact: every aggressive thinning tested cost accuracy. At equal cost, the selected layers outperform the four shifted windows tested. On 13 unseen low-redundancy scenes with 32 views, LMSA stays within 1.4 AUC@5 of dense attention, compared with 10.3 for AVGGT and 4.5 for SAF3R; its difference from contemporaneous GPA-VGGT is not significant, and only its gains over AVGGT pass both scene-level tests. With 100 views, it stays within 1.9 AUC@5 while its aggregator runs $2.0\times$ faster. Used post hoc to choose the layers GPA-VGGT protects, the statistic improves it by 1.2 AUC@5 for 5% more FLOPs. Applied untuned to $\pi^3$, it beats AVGGT but remains further from dense accuracy.|[2611.23554](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23554)|
|**2026-11-19**|**DOCK: Dual-Stream-Inspired Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representations Grounded in Robot Kinematics**|Pengju Liu et.al.|Latent-space planners select actions by comparing the embedding of a predicted future image with that of a goal image. This assumes that distance in the embedding reflects how far the scene is from the goal. We profile this assumption with simulator-executed futures, which removes prediction error. For six frozen DINO and V-JEPA encoders, feature distance barely tracks the object's distance to its goal: the rank correlation is at most 0.11, against 0.87 for object-mask centroids. It is dominated by background and robot patches, and frozen-feature readouts capture the arm far better than the object. Inspired by the ventral (what) and dorsal (where/how) visual streams, we propose DOCK, which learns an object representation whose changes agree with measured physical motion. A grasped object moves with the gripper, so forward kinematics on the joint angles gives a proxy for the object's displacement without annotation. From 9,951 held-object transport trajectories in 21 simulated kitchen scenes, we mine 404K displacement pairs and train three components: an object token pooled from patch features (what), a spatial ruler that makes differences of readout coordinates equal to measured displacements (where), and a dynamics predictor over object tokens (how). Used as a planning cost, the learned representation places the object in 15 of 21 tasks, as many as an oracle that reads the true object position, while mask geometry reaches 10 and frozen feature distance 9. It still solves the most tasks when the unseen robot arm is visible, and its ranking transfers to held-out layouts with unseen object instances and categories without any adaptation.|[2611.23578](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23578)|
|**2026-11-19**|**ExiST: Existence-Aware Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation**|Maxx Richard Rahman et.al.|Semi-supervised multi-organ segmentation should learn more than a dozen organs from a handful of labeled scans, and the smallest organs occupy less than one percent of the foreground. We identify a failure mode of self-training that is specific to this regime. When a teacher misses a small organ in a scan, every voxel of that organ receives the confident pseudo-label background, and the student is trained toward the organ absence. Repeated over many scans, this loop extinguishes tail organs. In a pilot study, removing the gallbladder from the pseudo-labels reduced its Dice on AMOS from 36.5 to 1.0. We argue that a missing organ should be treated as unresolved rather than absent and propose Existence-aware Self-Training (ExiST). It builds pseudo-labels by leave-one-out consensus of independently trained networks, screens them with a quality gate on validation scans, and infers, per scan and per organ, whether the organ was found. For every unresolved organ, the background voxels of that scan receive the set-valued target, trained with a marginal cross-entropy that accepts either answer and a Dice term that skips uncertain voxels. We show that this loss never pushes a candidate organ toward absence and never favors one member of the set, which leaves the decision to labeled evidence. ExiST outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods and reaches 77.1 mean Dice on Synapse with 20% labeled scans and 75.9 on AMOS with 5% labeled scans.|[2611.23581](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23581)|
|**2026-11-19**|**GRAFT: Graph-Regularized Prototype Fields for Realistic Test-Time Adaptation of VLMs**|Maxx Richard Rahman et.al.|Unlabeled test data can improve the zero-shot classifier of a vision-language model, yet transductive and test-time adaptation methods often fall below the zero-shot baseline when only a few vocabulary classes are present in a batch or when streams are correlated. We trace this failure to a shared design: every class owns independent parameters estimated from its own samples, so absent or rare classes are left at biased text anchors or fitted to foreign samples. We propose Graph-Regularized Anchor-displacement Field Transduction (GRAFT), which models the adapted prototypes as text anchors plus a displacement field that is partially pooled over a semantic class graph through a Gaussian Markov random field prior, together with an explicit class-presence model. Inference is closed-form and gradient-free on cached features. Anchor-only shrinkage and a single global shift are the two extreme settings of the prior; absent classes are provably harmonic extensions of the present ones, and the pooling strength can be chosen by empirical Bayes. Under the realistic batch and online protocols on eleven benchmarks and four ImageNet shifts, GRAFT improves over the zero-shot model in every setting and over anchor-based transduction where few classes are present.|[2611.23591](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23591)|
|**2026-11-19**|**VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters**|Shubing Yang et.al.|Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. We propose VIBRA, which matches relevance on the old gallery, corrects the errors of a single model with the barycenter of several views, which is itself a query in the old space, and trains the new encoder to inherit this consensus, so that models absent at deployment still shape every query. We show that the barycenter gains margin over the average of its views exactly when their hardest irrelevant items differ, and we characterize the share of this gain that one encoder can reach. On five benchmarks with five upgrades among six CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP2 backbones, VIBRA is the best compatible method in all 50 settings, improving Recall@1 by up to 5.6 points over the strongest baseline and by up to 18.0 points over the old model, while adding less than 1 ms to the latency of the new encoder.|[2611.23606](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23606)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair**|Avinash Goutham Aluguvelly et.al.|In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled rows in the projector and noise in the vision encoder of both models, infers the unknown scale factors, restores most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values, and returns accuracy to near its original level; programs that it writes from such weights repair unseen checkpoints of the same model without feedback. These repairs depend on a trace of how the faults were computed. The original weights have 16-bit precision, and faults computed in 32-bit arithmetic leave low bits that only the damaged weights carry. Rounding those bits away leaves each model's answers to our test questions unchanged, and the agent, unaided, then restores no weight exactly: on SmolVLM it no longer finds the damage, and in a single session on LFM2-VL its only gain comes from rescaling answer-token embeddings, which changes how often the model answers yes. Marking the damaged weights again in their low bits brings the edits back to them. Rounded weights still hold statistical evidence of the rescaling, in the distribution of stored values and in row norms, and one sentence in the prompt that names such a statistic directs the agent's edits to the damaged rows on both models. Swapped rows or columns, which leave the set of stored values unchanged, are not found unaided on either model within our session budgets. We recommend that studies of weight repair report the number format of the weights and include a rounded control.|[2611.23615](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23615)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Isthmus: Bridging Supervision Islands Restores Uncertainty and Stability in One-Step Flows**|Luming Yang et.al.|One-step flow maps are increasingly used as posterior samplers, where the point of sampling is the uncertainty that the samples carry. We find that the one-step sampler loses this uncertainty and becomes less stable. Compared with multi-step samples of the same network, its samples lose variance and decorrelate. Supervising the one-step jump directly makes this worse; the samples collapse further toward the conditional mean and break down when training is extended. We trace both failures to the locations where training places its pairs of start and end times. Only pairs on the diagonal of the time triangle receive targets from data, and the pair used for one-step sampling is either left unsupervised or supervised on an island, a set of pairs that the self-consistency identity does not connect to the diagonal, where the objective neither determines the one-step map nor anchors its training. We bridge the island with an isthmus, which places 5% of the training pairs along the whole edge of the triangle that joins the one-step pair to the diagonal. The error of the one-step map is then bounded by the self-consistency residual along this edge. With the network, the loss and the inference code unchanged and at no added cost, the isthmus improves one-step sampling across several flow-map objectives, in MRI reconstruction, face inpainting, and unconditional generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 32x32. On brain MRI, it restores one-step calibration to 0.96 and the correlation with multi-step samples to 0.93; both vary far less across seeds, and the agreement holds when training is extended to three times its length.|[2611.23616](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23616)|
|**2026-11-19**|**PRISM: Profiling and Representation of Individual Stereotypical Motion**|Austin A. MBaye et.al.|An anatomical pose provides interpretable joint structure, but no fixed set of physical landmarks can fully specify a person's movement. We introduce PRISM, a complementary representation that characterizes repetitive movement using tracked masks and dense optical flow. Torso-relative flow measures intensity, frame-wise mask variation measures spatial extent, signed-flow recurrence estimates frequency, and persistent sliding-window geometry describes the rhythmicity of the movement. Across 1,890 synthetic conditions, the measurements recover controlled speed, amplitude, and frequency while exposing observation limits. An idealized hand-motion experiment demonstrates variation omitted by identical exact COCO-17 trajectories; controlled corruption experiments separately examine measurement sensitivity. Audits of two pose methods on the same data cohort and 36,930 external skeleton clips document incomplete observation and dependence on processing choices. In 1,404 annotated complex stereotypical motor movement bouts from six autistic participants, total flow converges with pose motion, while matched-coordinate examples and repeated-session profiles show differences in intensity, extent, frequency, and rhythmicity within behavior labels. A separate VLM comparison evaluates quantitative frequency estimation, and a profile-conditioned decoder links the measurements to illustrative skeletal movements. PRISM connects numerical profiles to visible examples, providing an interpretable way to compare how the same behavior is expressed beyond its label or event count.|[2611.23646](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23646)|

|**2026-11-19**|**Mapping the Design Space of Feature Sampling for Optical Flow**|Liping Zhang et.al.|The computation of correlation features is crucial for optical flow estimation. |**2026-11-19**|**NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding**|Zhang Ziyue et.al.|Long video understanding remains a daunting challenge for existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs), mainly due to the large number of visual tokens accumulated in long videos. |**2026-11-19**|**Beyond Additive Composition: Interventional Modeling of State-Dependent Cross-Degradation Responses for Composite Image Restoration**|Zongda Tang et.al.|Composite image restoration aims to recover images corrupted by multiple coexisting degradations. |**2026-11-19**|**SimplePro: A Simple Baseline for Proactive Video Understanding**|Yilin Wang et.al.|Proactive video understanding requires vision-language models (VLMs) to decide not only what to answer as a video unfolds, but also when newly arrived evidence warrants a response and when to remain silent. |**2026-11-19**|**DORMS: Image Segmentation via Depth-Ordered Region Merge Trees**|Furkan Mumcu et.al.|We introduce DORMS (Depth-Ordered Region Merging for Segmentation), a purely algorithmic approach to image segmentation from monocular depth maps, requiring no neural networks or learned parameters in the segmentation process. |**2026-11-19**|**SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs**|Alin-Ionut Popa et.al.|Vision-language models (VLMs) grasp the overall content of an image but often miss the fine details a question hinges on, such as a small object in a large photo or a number in a dense infographic. |**2026-11-19**|**Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders**|Hongxu Chen et.al.|In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. |**2026-11-19**|**TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting**|Guanzhong Sun et.al.|Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. |**2026-11-19**|**Agreement Is Not Accuracy: LiDAR Elevation Errors Hidden in LiDAR-Camera Extrinsics**|Yeon Kun Lee et.al.|LiDAR and cameras provide complementary measurements for 3D vision, yet agreement between their observations does not establish the accuracy of either sensor's internal geometry. |**2026-11-19**|**SIRAZ: Sparse Inter-Layer Residual Aggregation for Zero-Shot Visual Neural Decoding**|Neha et.al.|Brain-computer interfaces aim to establish direct communication between neural activity and external systems, making interpretation of brain signals an important problem. |**2026-11-19**|**WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise**|Kaiwen Wang et.al.|Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. |**2026-11-19**|**ReSynth: Constructing Synthetic Supervision for Multi-Image Understanding**|Yilin Wang et.al.|People often understand the world by comparing different views of it. |**2026-11-19**|**ProtoBridge-CLIP: Observation-Masked Finding Prototypes for Medical Image--Report Representation Learning**|Jinrui Wu et.al.|Radiology reports distinguish affirmed findings, explicit negations, and unmentioned concepts, but conventional global image--report contrastive learning often compresses these different evidence states into a single study-level target. |**2026-11-19**|**Choosing Supervised Post-Processing for Frozen Person Detectors: Information, Object Changes, and Complete Cost**|Tianyi Zhou et.al.|A frozen detector computes hypotheses that can support better final outputs through supervised post-processing. |**2026-11-19**|**Freeforward4d: Annotation-free feed-forward 4d reconstruction of driving scenes**|Luosong Guo et.al.|Feed-forward 4D reconstruction enables efficient creation of renderable driving scenes for autonomous driving simulation. |**2026-11-19**|**HHW-Ego: DSLR-Quality Enhancement for Multi-Source Wearable Ego Imaging**|Yunfei Tong et.al.|Wearable ego-centric images are now in high demand for scenarios ranging from daily smart glass usage to embodied intelligence. |**2026-11-19**|**FlyVQA: Seeing Video Frame Interpolation Quality through Fly Eyes**|Baoliang Chen et.al.|The ultimate ambition of visual quality assessment is to reproduce the neural computations of human vision and thereby achieve full alignment with human perception. |**2026-11-19**|**Rethinking Contrastive Targets in Radiology Language-Image Pretraining**|Yunhe Gao et.al.|CLIP-style contrastive image-text pretraining is widely used in radiology data, where each image is paired with one report and every other report in the batch is treated as a negative. |**2026-11-19**|**Semi-Supervised GAN-Based Segmentation of CTPA Scans for Pulmonary Emboli Boundary Extraction**|Maria Thoma et.al.|Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a pulmonary vascular disease associated with high morbidity and mortality, where delayed diagnosis can be fatal. |**2026-11-19**|**STAR++: A Physical-Aware Benchmark and Framework for Astronomical Super-Resolution across Multiple Filters**|Guohang Zhuang et.al.|Astronomical super-resolution (ASR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution star fields from low-resolution telescope observations across multiple filters for astrophysical analysis. |**2026-11-19**|**Semantic-aware Contrasting with Explicitly Disentangled Representations for AI-Generated Video Detection**|Jiaquan Yu et.al.|The rapid proliferation of AI-generated videos (AIGVs) has raised critical concerns about content authenticity. |**2026-11-19**|**R $^{3}$ Sieve: Suppressing Unconditional Information from Attention to Answers for High-Resolution VQA**|Yifan Cao et.al.|High-resolution visual question answering (VQA) requires models to identify question-relevant small objects in high-resolution images and select the correct answer based on what they recognize, demanding fine-grained perception. |**2026-11-19**|**AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation**|Shiwei Wu et.al.|Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. |**2026-11-19**|**APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding**|Junxiang Wen et.al.|Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. |**2026-11-19**|**Learning Where and How Much to Sample: Volume-Adaptive k-Space Acquisition for Accelerated MRI**|Reyhaneh Neshatavar et.al.|Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential medical imaging technique, but its high costs and long acquisition times can limit accessibility. |**2026-11-19**|**From Restoration to Redrawing: Revitalizing Ancient Chinese Characters by SVG Code Generation and Editing**|Weiguang Zhang et.al.|Hanjian manuscripts written on Han Dynasty bamboo and wooden slips are invaluable heritage of ancient Chinese writing but suffer from damaged ink and incomplete strokes. |**2026-11-19**|**Object Pose: The Link between Weak Perspective, Paraperspective, and Full Perspective**|Radu Horaud et.al.|Recently, DeMenthon and Davis [4,5] proposed a method for determining the pose of a 3-D object with respect to a camera from 3-D to 2-D point correspondences. |**2026-11-19**|**RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models**|Ruisi Zhao et.al.|Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. |**2026-11-19**|**IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents**|Zhizhuo Kou et.al.|Organizations increasingly deploy downloaded open-weight GUI agents. |**2026-11-19**|**SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement**|Leyang Tao et.al.|Predicting the RNA and protein content of cells from routine H&E images could extend spatial molecular profiling to existing slide archives. |**2026-11-19**|**EVF-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for E-commerce Visual Effects in Video Generation**|Run Ling et.al.|E-commerce visual effects (EVF) are dynamic, product-centered visual presentations in e-commerce videos, often accompanied by promotional text. |**2026-11-19**|**How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?**|Yosuke Yamagishi et.al.|Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. |**2026-11-19**|**PatchAdaNet: Unsupervised class incremental learning using local patches and global adapters**|Kamel Aouaidjia et.al.|Biological learning systems acquire knowledge incrementally through broad, reusable representations established early and kept largely stable, while integrating new experience with minimal interference with previously learned knowledge. |**2026-11-19**|**Inherited Adapter Experts for Replay-Free Domain-Incremental Learning**|Gyutae Oh et.al.|Replay-free domain-incremental learning trains a model on the same classes in successive domains without keeping earlier images. |**2026-11-19**|**SEER: Semantic Evidence for Executable Region Propagation in Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation**|Junyang Chen et.al.|Training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) has made strong progress by adapting CLIP-like representations to dense prediction, but its remaining errors are often local, structured, and tied to the active label space. |**2026-11-19**|**Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development**|Xirui Jiang et.al.|Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. |**2026-11-19**|**GenRF: Generative Registration-free Image Fusion**|Linfeng Tang et.al.|Multi-modal image fusion combines complementary observations to improve scene visibility and perception. |**2026-11-19**|**AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination**|Xiaoqian Shen et.al.|Vision-Language Models increasingly rely on textual reasoning to solve advanced multimodal tasks. |**2026-11-19**|**Stabilizing Neural-to-Image Retrieval with Frequency-Domain Priors and Adaptive Supervision**|YaoYang Liu et.al.|Visual neural decoding aims to infer perceived visual stimuli from brain activity, offering important insights into human visual cognition while enabling transformative applications in brain computer interfaces and artificial intelligence. |**2026-11-19**|**ViStep-RL: Stepwise Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Visual Agents**|Junyang Chen et.al.|Long-horizon visual agents must do more than inspect images: they must turn observations into evidence that remains usable as a task unfolds. |**2026-11-19**|**ART: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer**|Zichen Zhang et.al.|3D affordance acts as a critical link between perception and action, providing priors for robotic manipulation. |**2026-11-19**|**Monitoring Unplanned Construction Using Satellite Change Detection**|Harsh Kashyap et.al.|Cities need land for homes, shops, roads, and public services. |**2026-11-19**|**From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation**|YaoYang Liu et.al.|Visually evoked EEG-to-text generation aims to produce natural-language descriptions from neural responses elicited by visual stimuli. |**2026-11-19**|**Target-Consistent Action Guidance via Semi-Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Drifting World Models**|Md Abtahi Majeed Chowdhury et.al.|Action-conditioned world models let robots imagine the outcomes of their actions for planning and offline policy evaluation, but these uses need many rollouts, which multi-step diffusion makes expensive. |**2026-11-19**|**Semantic Guidance for Joint Infrared-Visible Video Fusion and Frame Interpolation**|Yushen Xu et.al.|Infrared and visible video fusion at high frame rates requires recovering missing observations when camera rates differ or fall below the desired output rate. |**2026-11-19**|**AnchorUp: Anchoring Feature Upsampling on a Classical Interpolation**|Kotaro Horikawa et.al.|Vision foundation models produce semantically strong features on a coarse patch grid, and dense prediction needs them at pixel resolution. |**2026-11-19**|**CanopyKV: Remember beyond the Crop for Fast Active Visual Reasoning**|Lei Yang et.al.|Active visual reasoning enables multimodal models to answer challenging visual questions by gathering fine-grained evidence through iterative image inspection and tool use. |**2026-11-19**|**Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models**|Mohammad Mirzaee et.al.|In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. |**2026-11-19**|**Reliable Tree Recruitment from Scarce Annotations for Forest Inventory Expansion**|Luiz Fernando Souza Luz et.al.|Species-level inventories of individual tree crowns (ITCs) from UAV imagery are limited by annotation cost: in tropical forests, many species are represented by only a handful of field-validated crowns. |**2026-11-19**|**RAPID: Reconstruction Accelerated by Polarization-Informed Depth for 2D Gaussian Splatting**|Daisong Ouyang et.al.|Efficient and accurate 3D surface reconstruction from multi-view images remains a fundamental challenge in Gaussian splatting. |**2026-11-19**|**StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model**|Chuang Wang et.al.|Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. |**2026-11-19**|**Why Multi-Source Audio Fails to Compose: A Geometric Diagnosis and Its Remedy**|Anurag Singh et.al.|Multi-source audio-to-image generation exhibits consistent compositional failures when audio tokens occupy geometrically displaced, semantically unanchored positions in the CLIP text-token space, where the diffusion U-Net lacks the prior to reliably attend to them or ground them in distinct spatial regions. |**2026-11-19**|**PhysResponse: Probing the Physics of Video Generation with Controlled Interventions**|Yuhan Li et.al.|Video generation models are increasingly viewed as world simulators, which requires not only plausible motion but dynamics that respond correctly to specified physical parameters. |**2026-11-19**|**Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs**|Xiaolin Lin et.al.|Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about long interleaved inputs, such as documents of many pages and collections of hundreds of images, but they are slow to start: on inputs of about 100K tokens, the prefill takes most of the wait for the first output token. |**2026-11-19**|**MLIE-CoT: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Multi-Level Image Editing**|Baichuan Yang et.al.|Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has proven effective in improving the reasoning abilities of large language models by breaking complex tasks into step-by-step solutions. |**2026-11-19**|**Explainable and CPU-Efficient Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Using Two-Phase EfficientNetB3 Fine-Tuning**|Deepro Das et.al.|Brain tumors are among the most lethal neurological disorders, with over 308,000 new diagnoses annually worldwide. |**2026-11-19**|**NativeSeg: Native Vision Language Segmentation of 3D Computed Tomography via Spatial Visual Tokens and Verified Local Zoom**|Chengqian Ma et.al.|Text prompted 3D computed tomography (CT) segmentation requires both full slice context and fine boundary precision across volumes where over $80\%$ of organ prompted slices lack the queried target. |**2026-11-19**|**Retroactive Concept Bottleneck Models for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning**|Yang Ji et.al.|Exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) requires models to learn new classes sequentially without retaining training samples from previous tasks. |**2026-11-19**|**EviScope: Evidence-Conditioned Sampling for Long-Range 3D Detection**|Mingyang Lyu (Institute of Automation et.al.|Query-based camera-radar detectors choose where and over which frames each object query samples from the query's position or feature. |**2026-11-19**|**EgoJev: Finding Evidence in Egocentric Video by Reading VLM Decisions**|Chunggi Lee et.al.|Questions about long egocentric video often depend on one brief moment, such as the second a hand puts an object down. |**2026-11-19**|**AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection**|Zhi Li et.al.|Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or high annotation costs. |**2026-11-19**|**Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?**|Zijie Xin et.al.|Omni-modal large language models (omni-modal LLMs) can respond to spoken requests directly through voice and video calls. |**2026-11-19**|**Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping**|Ege Artan et.al.|The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover fractional abundances. |**2026-11-19**|**$Z$ -sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling**|Junjie Ye et.al.|We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. |**2026-11-19**|**Coarse-to-Fine Sparse Transformer for Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction**|Yuanhao Cai et.al.|Many algorithms have been developed to solve the inverse problem of coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI), i.e., recovering the 3D hyperspectral images (HSIs) from a 2D compressive measurement. |**2026-11-19**|**MST++: Multi-stage Spectral-wise Transformer for Efficient Spectral Reconstruction**|Yuanhao Cai et.al.|Existing leading methods for spectral reconstruction (SR) focus on designing deeper or wider convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn the end-to-end mapping from the RGB image to its hyperspectral image (HSI). An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST-plus-plus|[2204.07908](http://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07908)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Retinexformer: One-stage Retinex-based Transformer for Low-light Image Enhancement**|Yuanhao Cai et.al.|When enhancing low-light images, many deep learning algorithms are based on the Retinex theory. An online Gradio demo is available on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/Retinexformer|[2303.06705](http://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06705)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Binarized Spectral Compressive Imaging**|Yuanhao Cai et.al.|Existing deep learning models for hyperspectral image (HSI) reconstruction achieve good performance but require powerful hardwares with enormous memory and computational resources. An online Gradio demo is available on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST|[2305.10299](http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10299)|
|**2026-11-19**|**I2I Backdoor: Backdoor Attacks against Image-to-Image Tasks**|Wenbo Jiang et.al.|With the rapid development of deep learning technology, deep learning-based Image-to-Image (I2I) networks have become the predominant choice for I2I tasks like image super-resolution and denoising. |**2026-11-19**|**VerifyPrompt: Towards Text-to-Image Models Verification Behind Black-Box APIs**|Ji Guo et.al.|With the rise of diverse Text-to-Image (T2I) models such as DALL-E 3, third-party platforms increasingly integrate multiple black-box APIs to deliver cost-effective services. |**2026-11-19**|**Quicksviewer: An LMM with Early Video Compression using Annealed Gumbel-Softmax**|Ji Qi et.al.|Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) uniformly perceive video frames, creating computational inefficiency for videos with inherently varying temporal redundancy. |**2026-11-19**|**FedS2R: One-Shot Federated Domain Generalization for Synthetic-to-Real Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving**|Tao Lian et.al.|Federated domain generalization has shown promising progress in image classification by enabling collaborative training across multiple clients without sharing raw data. |**2026-11-19**|**EgoControl: Controllable Egocentric Video Generation via 3D Full-Body Poses**|Enrico Pallotta et.al.|Egocentric video generation with fine-grained control through body motion is a key requirement towards embodied AI agents that can simulate, predict, and plan actions. |**2026-11-19**|**CausalSpatial: A Benchmark for Object-Centric Causal Spatial Reasoning**|Wenxin Ma et.al.|Humans can look at a static scene and instantly predict what happens next -- will moving this object cause a collision? |**2026-11-19**|**Multimodal Information Fusion for Chart Understanding: A Survey of MLLMs -- Evolution, Limitations, and Cognitive Enhancement**|Zhihang Yi et.al.|Chart understanding is a quintessential information fusion task, requiring the seamless integration of graphical and textual data to extract meaning. |**2026-11-19**|**How Far Does Online RL Generalize in Mobile GUI Agents? |**2026-11-19**|**CURVAS-PDACVI: A Multi-Rater CT Dataset and Challenge for Pancreatic Cancer Segmentation and Vascular Involvement Assessme**|M. |**2026-11-19**|**TEA: Text Encoder Alignment for Robust Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models**|Alireza Dehghanpour Farashah et.al.|Text-to-image diffusion models can be misused to generate harmful content through adversarial or paraphrased prompts that bypass built-in safety mechanisms. |**2026-11-19**|**MVC-Bench: Benchmarking Calibration of Medical Vision-Language Models**|Ashshak Sharifdeen et.al.|Reliable evaluation of vision-language models (VLMs) and medical vision-language models (Medical-VLMs) requires calibrated confidence, particularly under realistic clinical conditions. |**2026-11-19**|**Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models**|Ziyue Wang et.al.|On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has recently emerged as an effective post-training paradigm that provides dense token-level supervision from a privileged self-teacher, yet it remains underexplored for Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs). |**2026-11-19**|**Visual Token Coding for Video Multimodal Large Language Models**|Chenxin Fang et.al.|In this paper, we propose a new token compression paradigm for video Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), termed Visual Token Coding ($VTC$). |**2026-11-19**|**RadMatch: Auditable Radiology Report Evaluation via Finding-Level Matching**|Charles Corbi\`ere et.al.|As AI systems are increasingly used to draft radiology reports, reliably evaluating their clinical quality remains a critical challenge. |**2026-11-19**|**Adapting a Foundation Model for Lunar Surface Height Estimation**|Patrick Bauer et.al.|Digital elevation models (DEMs) can provide accurate height information, making it invaluable for analyzing the lunar surface. |**2026-11-19**|**OracleZoom: Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super-Resolution Beyond Ground Truth**|Shubhashis Roy Dipta et.al.|Recursive image Super-Resolution (SR) reaches extreme magnification by feeding each prediction back into the same model, like zooming into an image again and again. |**2026-11-19**|**Synthetic Leprosy Image Generation Using Mask-Conditioned Latent Diffusion and Transfer Learning from Large Chronic Wound Datasets**|Yusuf Abdulkadir et.al.|Machine learning for neglected tropical diseases is limited by data, not algorithms: public annotated image sets for leprosy (Hansen's disease) number in the hundreds. |**2026-11-19**|**Small Object Detection in Drone Aerial Imagery with LAF-YOLOv10**|Quratulain Nayeem et.al.|General-purpose object detectors lose accuracy on UAV footage, where targets span only a handful of pixels and onboard compute is limited. |**2026-11-19**|**Rethinking the Reconstruction-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders**|Hongyang Du et.al.|Fusing shallower encoder layers into a Representation Autoencoder (RAE) sharpens pixel reconstruction but degrades diffusion generation. |**2026-11-19**|**Difficulty-Aware Statistical Matching for Dataset Distillation**|Hongxu Ma et.al.|Dataset distillation (DD) condenses a large original set into a small distilled set with high training utility. |**2026-11-19**|**An Invariant Tangent-Angle Descriptor and a Band U-Net for 2D Fragment Adjacency Prediction**|Guillaume Brouillette (Universit\'e du Qu\'ebec \`a Trois-Rivi\`eres et.al.|Reassembling a broken artefact begins with deciding which fragments are adjacent. |**2026-11-19**|**Scenes as an Attack Surface: Uncovering Scene-Grounded Safety Failures in MLLMs**|Tongxi Wu et.al.|Existing jailbreak attacks have exposed serious safety weaknesses in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). |**2026-11-19**|**Graphene: A Lightweight Transformer with Ising Mean-Field Refinement for Image Super-Resolution**|Seungki Hong et.al.|This paper proposes Graphene, a lightweight image super-resolution architecture with two complementary feature refinement mechanisms: Ising-model-inspired local feature refinement using an Ising Refinement Block (IRB) and stage-history-based feature refinement using a History Attention (HistAttn) module. |**2026-11-19**|**BlockAlign: Preference Optimization for Trajectory-Distilled Video Generation**|Jingyuan Zhu et.al.|Directly aligning trajectory-distilled video generators slashes rollout costs and optimizes the deployed few-step model without teacher fine-tuning or re-distillation. |**2026-11-19**|**Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry**|Aydin Mohseni et.al.|One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. And when AI variants that keep more resources spread faster, alignment lasts only while misaligned variants are reliably sanctioned. In these two senses, human-AI mutualism is unstable.|[2611.23322](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23322)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight**|Alex Lin Wang et.al.|Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. On five held-out oversight evaluations, an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming honesty training (0.864), transcript monitoring (0.828), and activation oracles (0.796). We further find that training an observer makes the assistant itself easier to monitor, with every baseline method improving on average when applied to the fine-tuned assistant. These results suggest that training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves is a tractable approach to overseeing unintended behavior.|[2611.23365](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23365)|
|**2026-11-19**|**Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding**|Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik et.al.|Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the requested edits to where they began, with each direction started from a stored reference tree, and the spread of its cost over repeated cycles defines a software temperature, which rose with the sampling temperature of the model. About 80 per cent of the tokens of a successful run are generated in model calls that leave the requested change where it was, and we call these tokens heat. The free energy of a change, which we estimate by analogy with the equality of Jarzynski, is 14 to 22 per cent of the mean cost of a successful coding run. Coding costs 1.1 to 1.5 times as much as uncoding. The daemon is imperfect: the verdict of a test suite varies with its environment, and a suite that accepts a broken change has a cost in tokens. The practical implication of the proposed theory could be new tools for analysing and optimising coding agents through the lens of thermodynamics.|[2611.23375](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23375)|

|**2026-11-19**|**BOS Summary: The First Token Matters**|Hui Zhu et.al.|Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. |**2026-11-19**|**GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design**|Sevda Ebrahimi et.al.|Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. |**2026-11-19**|**BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing**|Malak Gamal El-Din et.al.|Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. |**2026-11-19**|**FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives**|Balakrishnan Arumugam et.al.|Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. |**2026-11-19**|**Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance**|Kaiwen Shi et.al.|Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. |**2026-11-19**|**ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents**|Jiangyun Zhang et.al.|Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. |**2026-11-19**|**RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution**|Adhyayan Veer Singh et.al.|Tool runtimes can lower an agent-selected operation into a hidden parallel graph, reducing latency and context while risking semantic mistranslation. |**2026-11-19**|**Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities**|Song Young Oh et.al.|In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. |**2026-11-19**|**Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics**|Dowling Wong et.al.|Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. |**2026-11-19**|**Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents**|Tiancheng Bao et.al.|Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. |**2026-11-19**|**KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch**|Zhuo Chen et.al.|The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. |**2026-11-19**|**Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents**|Jinbae Seo et.al.|Multimodal agents largely rely on generic tools such as cropping, search, and code execution, leaving specialist vision models outside their tool space. |**2026-11-19**|**GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs**|Zhi Sheng et.al.|Accurate forecasting of order volume at scale-effect hotspots (SEHs), spatially coherent groups of logistics flows that serve as distributed optimization units for real-time many-to-one dispatch, is a prerequisite for efficient order pooling in on-demand food delivery (OFD) platforms such as Meituan. |**2026-11-19**|**SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills**|Nami Cho et.al.|An agent skill that succeeded yesterday may be executable today without being justified for reuse today. |**2026-11-19**|**Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure**|Behrooz Tahmasebi et.al.|Test-time compute has emerged as a powerful way to improve the accuracy of language models at inference time, with scaling laws quantifying how accuracy improves with additional forward passes. |**2026-11-19**|**MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain**|Sara Amar et.al.|We introduce MANGO Arena, an open-source testbed in which four LLM agents each run one company in a serial supply chain adapted from MANGO, a classroom factory-management game. |**2026-11-19**|**DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination**|Ziyi Jiao et.al.|Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. |**2026-11-19**|**Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights**|Jiajun Fan et.al.|A language model is trained once and frozen. |**2026-11-19**|**Improving Outdoor Multi-cell Fingerprinting-based Positioning via Mobile Data Augmentation**|Tony Chahoud et.al.|Accurate outdoor positioning in cellular networks is hindered by sparse, heterogeneous measurement collections and the high cost of exhaustive site surveys. |**2026-11-19**|**TinyMyo: a Tiny Foundation Model for Flexible EMG Signal Processing at the Edge**|Matteo Fasulo et.al.|Objective: Surface electromyography (EMG) is widely used in biomechanics, rehabilitation, prosthetic control, and human-machine interfaces. |**2026-11-19**|**Meta-RL with Bayesian Linear Task Models**|Jingyang You et.al.|Deep Bayesian reinforcement learning adapts to unseen tasks by inferring latent transition and reward models, but existing methods typically rely on variational posteriors and evidence lower bounds, introducing approximation error and unstable task representations. |**2026-11-19**|**Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective**|Saptarshi Roy et.al.|In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. |**2026-11-19**|**Disentangling generalization and memorization in large language models using chess**|Leonard S. Pleiss et.al.|Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities, yet it remains unclear to what extent these reflect sophisticated recall or genuine reasoning ability. |**2026-11-19**|**CoreQ: Mismatch-Corrected Successive Rounding for LLM Quantization**|Seohyeon Cha et.al.|Post-training quantization (PTQ) enables efficient deployment of large language models by mapping pretrained weights to low-bit formats without retraining, typically using a small calibration set to minimize a layer-wise calibration objective. |**2026-11-19**|**PANC: Prior-Aware Normalized Cut for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation**|Juan Guti\'errez et.al.|We study training-free in-context segmentation with externally annotated context priors: given a target image and a small set of foreground/background tokens extracted from annotated context images, the goal is to segment the corresponding target concept without training, fine-tuning, or target-image clicks. |**2026-11-19**|**Generating Adversarial Events: A Motion-Aware Point Cloud Framework**|Hongwei Ren et.al.|Event cameras have been widely adopted in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving, robotics, and human-computer interaction. |**2026-11-19**|**Multimodal Information Fusion for Chart Understanding: A Survey of MLLMs -- Evolution, Limitations, and Cognitive Enhancement**|Zhihang Yi et.al.|Chart understanding is a quintessential information fusion task, requiring the seamless integration of graphical and textual data to extract meaning. |**2026-11-19**|**Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems**|Mason Nakamura et.al.|Multi-agent systems, where LLM agents communicate through free-form language, enable sophisticated coordination for solving complex cooperative tasks. |**2026-11-19**|**PEARL: Personalized Streaming Video Understanding with Runtime-Defined Concepts**|Yuanhong Zheng et.al.|Unlike humans, who learn new concepts from a continuous visual stream, existing personalized vision-language models (VLMs) internalize a predefined concept set during training and operate on static images or offline videos. |**2026-11-19**|**MedExAgent: Training LLM Agents to Ask, Examine, and Diagnose in Noisy Clinical Environments**|Yicheng Gao et.al.|Real-world clinical diagnosis is a complex process in which the doctor is required to obtain information from both interaction with the patient and conducting medical exams.
